testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When you start a truck with a trailer, how do you know the ABS is not working?

options.text: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the right side of the trailer flashes three times.
All the rear lights flash and then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: When you start your engine, the dash lights should turn on and then off. If the ABS warning light stays on, the system is not working. On a truck with a trailer, if the yellow light on the left rear stays on after you start the engine, the ABS is not working properly.

questions.question: Why can parked delivery trucks be dangerous?

options.text: People may be in a hurry when leaving the truck and may not check for other vehicles.
Packages often fall out of the trucks into the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: People may be in a hurry when leaving the truck and may not check for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Parked delivery trucks can be dangerous. The driver may be in a hurry and pull into traffic without warning. They may also step out of the vehicle without checking for other traffic.

questions.question: What is removed when you drain an air tank?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have drains in the air tanks to remove water and compressor oil. If water and oil build up in the system, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This warns other drivers that you are stopped.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe amount of play on a 20-inch steering wheel?
questions.explanation: A steering wheel with more than 10 degrees of play may be defective. On a 20-inch wheel, 10 degrees equals about two inches of movement at the rim.

questions.question: If you are not sure how to put out a fire, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you are unsure how to put out a fire, wait for firefighters to arrive. Let them handle it. This is especially important with fires involving hazardous materials.

questions.question: When doing a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?

options.text: Always follow the same steps in the same order.
Do not worry about small mechanical problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always follow the same steps in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you remember all the important items to check and makes it less likely you will forget something.

questions.question: You should always drive so your vehicle can stop:

options.text: Within 10 feet of your current position.
Within 1,000 feet of your current position.
Within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within the distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Always drive at a speed where you can stop your vehicle completely within the area of road you can see ahead of you.

questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, brake drums should have no cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums during your walk-around inspection before each trip. It is unsafe to drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an effect of drinking alcohol and then driving?
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs driving and causes errors such as straddling lanes, jerky starts, not signaling, running stop signs and red lights, and improper passing. Alcohol slows your reaction time—it does not speed it up.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and sleep. This is the only safe action. Trying to fight fatigue and keep driving is very dangerous and can cause a deadly crash. Pills may keep you awake for a short time, but they will not make you more alert.

questions.question: What does rough acceleration do?
questions.explanation: Always speed up slowly and smoothly so your vehicle does not jerk. Rough acceleration can damage your engine.

questions.question: Which agency conducts the threat assessment for a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) conducts the threat assessment for applicants seeking a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: What is one way to handle blind spots?

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles so they cannot pass you.
Drive in the left lane so you only worry about vehicles on your right.
Check your mirrors often and watch where other vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often and watch where other vehicles are.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see the traffic around you. This helps you notice if other vehicles are moving into your blind spots.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake, the parking brake, and the emergency brake. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: Two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.
One air brake system with two different sets of controls.
One system for the left side of the truck and one for the right side, each with its own controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. One system usually controls the regular brakes on the rear axle while the other controls the regular brakes on the front axle.

questions.question: Which of these can result in being denied a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: You are not a lawful permanent resident of the United States.
You had a speeding ticket in the past three years.
You did not answer every question correctly on the test.
You did not pass the test on your first try.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are not a lawful permanent resident of the United States.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if you renounce your U.S. citizenship, are not a lawful permanent resident, are wanted or indicted for certain felonies, are judged mentally defective, are committed to a mental institution, or are deemed a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, what can drivers do to check the vehicle's position?

options.text: Are encouraged not to exit the vehicle.
Can exit only if the vehicle is in reverse.
Can exit if the vehicle is in neutral with the parking brake set.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can exit if the vehicle is in neutral with the parking brake set.
questions.explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, put the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake before leaving it to check its position. You can check the position twice, but only once during the straight line backing exercise.

questions.question: What does ABS allow you to do?
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) helps prevent your wheels from locking during hard braking. Drive and brake the same way with or without ABS.

questions.question: What is an encroachment during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: The vehicle crossing over a boundary line.
A driver making one pull-up movement.
A driver putting the vehicle in neutral and setting the parking brake.
The vehicle stalling while shifting gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle crossing over a boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment is when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during the test. Each encroachment counts as one error.

questions.question: A ramp's posted speed limit:

options.text: Works for some vehicles, but may be too fast for a large truck.
Is just a suggestion and can be exceeded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Works for some vehicles, but may be too fast for a large truck.
questions.explanation: Speed limits on exit and entrance ramps are set for cars. Large or heavily-loaded trucks need to go slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: The center of gravity in a trailer should be:

options.text: At the rear of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Keep cargo weight as low as possible. A center of gravity that is too high increases the risk of rollover.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, drivers must check cargo securement every:
questions.explanation: Check cargo securement before the trip starts, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: If you are turning left and there are two left turn lanes, which lane should you use?

options.text: Trucks should not turn where there are two left turn lanes.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles need extra space to turn left. When an intersection has two left turn lanes, use the right lane to start your turn.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air:

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the system and needs to be fixed by a mechanic.

questions.question: What can happen if parking brakes are used in wet weather with freezing temperatures?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and lock the vehicle in place.
The brakes may suddenly release on their own.
The brakes may become too smooth to work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and lock the vehicle in place.
questions.explanation: Do not use parking brakes in wet weather below freezing. The brakes could freeze and prevent the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: When traveling down a hill:

options.text: Your speed will stay the same.
You will come to a stop.

questions.explanation: When traveling downhill, gravity pulls the vehicle faster, causing speed to increase.

questions.question: Lights that show anti-lock brakes are not working are:
questions.explanation: Vehicles with anti-lock brakes have yellow warning lights that show when there is a problem with the brake system.

questions.question: You can identify a distracted driver if they are:
questions.explanation: A distracted driver may drift between lanes, change speeds often, use a cell phone, look at a map, eat, or talk with passengers.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab because of:

options.text: Using the wrong type of fuel.
Not enough oil in the engine.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you when you need to brake?

options.text: Tap your brakes a few times.
Stick your arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes a few times.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to make your brake lights flash. This warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: How does a vehicle's center of gravity affect driving?

options.text: It usually has no impact on how the vehicle handles.
It plays a large role in how safely a driver can handle the vehicle.
It should not be a concern when loading the vehicle.
It should only be a concern if the route has many hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It plays a large role in how safely a driver can handle the vehicle.
questions.explanation: A vehicle's center of gravity is very important for safe handling. Always place cargo as low as possible to keep the center of gravity low.

questions.question: What will the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: How quickly you reach your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on specific driving moves and your general driving behavior. You must drive safely and responsibly. Follow all traffic signs, signals, and laws. Do not cause an accident or commit a moving violation.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, when should your four-way flashers be on?

options.text: Only near railroad tracks if a train is approaching.

questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way flashers as you approach and cross a railroad crossing. Turn them off after your entire vehicle has crossed the tracks.

questions.question: Why is improperly loaded cargo a problem?

options.text: It reduces stress on the trailer frame.
It is unsafe, but will not damage the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Proper cargo loading is essential for safety. Unsecured cargo can fall and cause injury or death. Poor loading can damage your vehicle and make it hard to steer safely.

questions.question: What is the rule for commercial drivers using cell phones?

options.text: You can use any cell phone while driving.
You can only use a hands-free cell phone while driving, if permitted.
You can only use a cell phone on rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only use a hands-free cell phone while driving, if permitted.
questions.explanation: You may only use a hands-free cell phone located close to you. Even hands-free phones can be distracting while driving. Know all cell phone laws in the state where you are driving.

questions.question: If ice forms on your side mirror, what does this mean?

options.text: The roadway probably has ice on it too.
The roadway will not have ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: The roadway probably has ice on it too.
questions.explanation: If ice forms on your mirrors or windshield wipers while you are driving, expect ice on the road surface as well.

questions.question: What is hydroplaning?

options.text: When tires lose grip on the road.
When tires gain more grip on the road.
When front tires grip better than rear tires.
When front tires grip less than rear tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tires lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens on wet roads when tires lose grip and slide along on a layer of water.

questions.question: What should you do if there is heavy fog on the road?
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is dangerous. Avoid driving when there is fog if possible.

questions.question: How long should it take for oil pressure to reach a normal level after starting the engine?
questions.explanation: Check your gauges when you start the engine. Oil pressure should reach a normal level within seconds of starting the vehicle.

questions.question: What affects stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on how fast you are driving. The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop.

questions.question: What happens when only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: The brakes will not work as well without ABS.
The brakes will become more sensitive.

questions.explanation: If the tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, jackknifing is less likely. The driver can still steer and control the vehicle.

questions.question: Which one does NOT cause hydraulic brake failure?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure happens when you lose pressure or when brakes overheat on long hills. Downshifting does not cause brake failure.

questions.question: On a vehicle with power steering, the hoses should be:
questions.explanation: When inspecting power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: What are tie-downs used for?
questions.explanation: Tie-downs secure cargo on flatbeds and in vans. They stop cargo from shifting or falling during driving. Shifting cargo can affect how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must:

options.text: Explain what you are inspecting and why
Estimate the weight of a load

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you are inspecting and why
questions.explanation: You must do a complete vehicle inspection. Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: Front tire tread depth must be at least ____ in every major groove.
questions.explanation: Front tires must have 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every major groove. Other tires need 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: Tell the motor carrier about problems that need repair
Make sure the vehicle is inspected regularly
Hold people accountable for inspecting the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the motor carrier about problems that need repair
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report tells the carrier about any problems that need to be fixed.

questions.question: A truck should be parked so that:

options.text: It must be backed up to leave
It can be pulled forward to leave

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be pulled forward to leave
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Park where you can pull forward when you leave.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, the driver should:

options.text: Not read it and find issues themselves
Take the vehicle to a mechanic
Skip the pre-trip inspection and use only the report

questions.explanation: Start your vehicle inspection by reading the last inspection report. The carrier should have fixed any problems listed in the report.
